title: Ops Buyers Negotiation Template — Dedicated Isolation & SLA
body:
Executive summary:

Purpose: give field sellers and solutions engineers a compact, procurement-facing negotiation template focused on Dedicated capacity: isolation guarantees, predictable throughput SLAs, and practical leverage points that map to engineering constraints. This doc is meant to be operational: cut-and-paste clauses, sample email asks, and a buyer objection scorecard.

Key selling pillars (one-liners):
- Predictable throughput: commit-backed capacity and burst model to avoid throttling during critical windows.
- Isolation: single-tenant GPU pools and tenant-aware tenancy to limit noisy neighbors and ensure performance stability.
- Measurable SLAs: latency and availability targets with transparent measurement windows and credit calculation.
- Operational guarantees: dedicated monitoring, escalation path, and playbooks for incident remediation.

Primary buyer personas and their top priorities:
- Platform/Infra Lead (Platform Architects): care about isolation, predictable tail latency, ability to pin model versions and dedicated kernels. Ask: how do you ensure no cross-tenant interference?
- ML Engineering Manager: cares about throughput for batch scoring and latency for interactive features. Ask: how do you scale model variants and fallbacks?
- Procurement/Legal: wants simple, auditable SLA definitions and clear credit math; cares about termination and liability.

Negotiation playbook (practical steps):
1) Discovery: capture peak QPS, P95/P99 latency SLAs, critical windows (cron jobs, events). Get model sizes and token budgets.
2) Propose commitment band: baseline reserved GPUs (X units), burst credits (Y tokens/hr), and optional canary capacity.
3) Map to guarantees: commit -> throughput floor; burst -> temporary headroom with transparent throttling policy.
4) Offer measurable SLA: availability (monthly uptime %) and latency SLO per route (e.g., 95% of calls < 120ms).
5) Contract language: use short, exact definitions (measurement windows, acceptable maintenance windows, exclusion events).
6) Concessions ladder: trade-offs we can offer vs ask: price discounts for longer commits, shorter SLA measurement windows for higher credits, or capacity isolation add-ons.

Sample SLA framing (plug-and-play language sellers can paste):
"Service Commitment: Redwood will maintain Dedicated Capacity such that committed throughput (measured as successful inference requests per minute using the customer’s pinned model version) is available at a baseline of {X} inference requests per minute (RPM) per reserved unit and a 99.0% availability target per calendar month. Latency Commitment: For requests routed to Dedicated capacity with model variant {model-id}, 95% of requests will observe server-side processing latency less than {T95} ms, measured at the edge egress. Failure to meet availability or latency targets will result in Service Credits as defined below."

SLA measurement & credit calculation (recommended):
- Measurement window: monthly, UTC.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows provided >=72 hours notice, force majeure, customer-originated network issues.
- Credit tiers: 99.9%+ = 0 credits; 99.0%–99.9% = 5% monthly credit; 98.0%–99.0% = 15%; <98.0% = 30% (caps at 100% of monthly reserved fee).
- Latency breach credit: per-route credits scaled to affected portion of committed RPM. Keep math simple and citable.

Isolation guarantees (technical commitments to be explicit about):
- Physical/Soft Isolation: Dedicated GPU pools are logically isolated; tenant scheduling prevents cross-tenant co-scheduling on the same physical GPU for reserved pools.
- Noisy-neighbor remediation SLA: If the customer reports reproducible performance degradation attributable to co-tenancy, Redwood will provide a remediation plan within 4 business hours and temporary migration/priority scheduling until resolved.
- Auditability: monthly usage and contention report available via Console and CSV export.

Operational attachments (what we include with Dedicated contracts):
- Onboarding checklist: account setup, model pinning, test harness for acceptance, synthetic load script.
- Escalation matrix: named contacts for support, SRE runbook snippets, and expected SLAT response times.
- Observability contract: retention windows for traces and token-level cost breakdown tied to committed units.

Competitive differentiation points (how to argue vs cloud provider endpoints and other inference vendors):
- Versus large cloud provider managed endpoints: we provide model-aware batching and quantization recommendations tuned for LLM semantics (better unit economics and lower tail latency for large seqs).
- Versus pure self-hosted runtimes: we provide a unified SLA + playbook and on-call escalation; buyers get the economics of managed support without building SRE+serving infra.
- Versus competitor X (example): competitor X guarantees throughput per vCPU unit but not per-GPU latency; highlight Redwood’s GPU-aware scheduling and model-level kernel selection.

Buyer objection scorecard (common objections and scripted responses):
- "We can self-host cheaper": acknowledge, then list total cost of ownership items — hiring SREs, kernel tuning, regression testing, and ongoing reliability. Offer a short pilot (30–60 days) to demonstrate delta.
- "Your SLA isn't strict enough": ask which metric they need tightened; propose targeted add-ons (e.g., shorter measurement windows, higher credits, 24/7 dedicated SRE) and price accordingly.
- "We need more data residency/compliance controls": map to Private deployment or VPC options and show integration path and timeline.

Negotiation levers and packaging suggestions (items we can trade):
- Term length: 12/24/36 months with stepped discounts.
- Tiered reserved units: baseline + optional burst pool that is billed only when used.
- Paid on-call SRE retainer for guaranteed MTTR SLAs.
- Observability add-ons: long retention, log export, and token-level billing snapshots.

Sample procurement-ready asks (email snippet to buyer/procurement):
"Hi <Procurement Name>,
Following our conversation, attached is our proposed Dedicated Capacity commitment and SLA summary: reserved units: {X}, burst credits: {Y}, latency target T95={T95}ms, monthly uptime target 99.0%. We’ve included the measurement definition and exemptions. Happy to walk through adjustments; if you need alternate credit bands, tell us which threshold you require and we will price it.
Best,
<Kiran>"

Risk scenarios and mitigation language to use with Legal:
- Risk: model upgrades cause unexpected latency regressions.
  Mitigation: include a rollback and canary policy in contract; define notice period for major model changes and automatic fallback policies to a pinned model version until validation completes.
- Risk: network egress spikes during large batches.
  Mitigation: define burst credit caps and optional egress-protected routes with traffic shaping.

Acceptance criteria for go/no-go (internal checklist sellers use before signing):
- Engineering has validated baseline workload with synthetic harness and achieved committed RPM in staging.
- Monitoring hooks instrumented and accessible to customer (read-only) during pilot.
- Contract includes agreed measurement windows, credit math, and exclusions.

Appendix: quick negotiation cheat-sheet (one-line bullets):
- If buyer asks for lower price, ask for longer term or larger commit.
- If buyer insists on zero exclusions, push for higher price or operational retainer.
- For enterprise audits/due diligence, offer short technical dry-run with SRE and a 1-week performance report.

Open questions for leadership and engineering (for internal review):
- Are the proposed credit tiers acceptable to Finance? (ask: cap on cumulative credits?)
- Can serving runtime guarantee eviction-free reserved pools at the promised commit levels?
- What's the maximum realistic burst capacity we can promise without manual intervention?

Next steps (owner: Kiran):
- Share this doc with Solutions Eng and Pricing for feedback by 2025-03-07.
- Draft a one-page slide with SLA bullets and sample contract language for AE use.
- Create a 30-day pilot template with onboarding checklist and synthetic harness.

Version: v0.9-draft

Notes to buyers/sellers: this template is deliberately prescriptive to reduce negotiation cycles. Tweak the variables (X/Y/T95) to match customer workload; engineering sign-off is required for any change to commit or burst definitions.
